title: Running for a uniform
news: Thousands of Jharkhand women, many young mothers, ran trials in sarees and shorts for a few Home Guard posts, backed by husbands who coached them and families who minded children.
syllabus: Social influence and attitude change; Gender justice
link: Women's work needs a change of attitude at home as much as jobs outside; supportive husbands and families show how social influence can widen women's choices.
question: How can families and communities change attitudes that limit women's participation in paid work? Illustrate with examples.

title: An institution that chose to listen
news: FIDE surveyed women chess players and found 76% had faced discrimination or harassment; its women's panel chair admits reporting systems must improve.
syllabus: Ethics of care in organisations · Gender justice · Work culture
link: Institutional care means seeking out uncomfortable truths about one's own organisation and building systems people trust.
question: As head of a national sports federation, you receive informal reports of harassment of women athletes, but no formal complaints. What steps will you take, and why?

title: Keralam makes elder care a right
news: Keralam passed India's first state law giving senior citizens enforceable rights to care and dignity.
syllabus: Empathy, tolerance and compassion towards the weaker sections
link: Dignity in old age moves from charity to entitlement; the state supports the family's duty rather than replacing it.
question: Is care of the elderly a family duty or a responsibility of the state? Discuss in the light of dignity and compassion.

title: Counting what women carry
news: The Statistics Ministry will measure women-specific constraints, such as household duties, in its survey of informal businesses.
syllabus: Social justice and gender · Evidence-based, ethical governance
link: What is not measured is rarely addressed: equity begins by making unpaid care work visible.
question: 'What is not counted does not count.' Discuss in the context of women's unpaid work and public policy.
